column1: # Verbs that take an indirect object written as a + noun phrase: the person
# or thing that receives, is told, is asked or is affected (dare il libro a
# Maria, telefonare a Maria, piacere a Marco). A dative clitic can stand for
# it (le do il libro, le telefono, gli piace). Only after these verbs does
# the grammar read an a phrase as an indirect object (vp.a-indirect-object);
# the a phrase keeps its adverbial reading too (dare il libro a casa), so a
# sentence where both fit is ambiguous. A place (andare a Roma), an object
# that ci stands for (pensare a Maria), a + infinitive and fixed activities
# (giocare a calcio) are not indirect objects.
# One verb per line as the infinitive without -si/-ne (rivolgersi ->
# rivolgere), then where the evidence comes from, then for model-proposed
#   wiktionary-sense    a sense note "[with a 'to someone']" or "[with a]" in
#                       where the a phrase is a person or thing a dative clitic
#   wiktionary-example  a Wiktionary usage example with the verb + a + a person
#   tatoeba             a sentence of homograph-set.jsonl has the verb with
#                       a + a person as its indirect object
#                       proposed by a language model (Claude Opus), with the
#                       example phrase in the third column, and accepted by a
#                       second, independent model (Claude Sonnet) that saw only
#                       the list and rejected 9 of 68 proposals (2026-11-14)
